Title: Composer / Lyricist
"Minuit, Chrétiens" ("Cantique de Noël"): lyrics: Placide Cappeau, music: Adolphe Adam
"Petit Papa Noël": lyrics: Raymond Vincy; music: Henri Martinet
"C'est Noël": lyrics: Jean Manse; music: Henri Betti

Title: Year published
"Çà, bergers, assemblons-nous": music 15th/16th century; published 1701 with words by Simon-Joseph Pellegrin
"Venez divin Messie": music 16th century; published 18th century with words by Simon-Joseph Pellegrin

Title: Notes
"Noel Bourguignon" ("Burgundian Carol"): Translated into English by Oscar Brand
"Il est né, le divin Enfant": Translated into English as "He Is Born, the Divine Christ Child"
"Les Anges dans nos campagnes": Translated into English as "Angels We Have Heard on High"
"Minuit, Chrétiens" ("Cantique de Noël"): Translated into English as "O Holy Night"
"Noël nouvelet": Translated into English as "Sing We Now of Christmas"
"Patapan" ("Guillô, pran ton tamborin!"): Title translation: Willy, take your tambourine
"C'est Noël": Song written for the movie Honoré de Marseille with Fernandel
"Quelle est cette odeur agréable?": Translated into English as "Whence Is That Goodly Fragrance Flowing?"
"Un flambeau, Jeannette, Isabelle": Translated into English as "Bring a Torch, Jeanette, Isabella"
"La Marche Des Rois Mages": Translated into English as "March of the Kings"
"Entre le bœuf et l'âne gris": Title translation: "Between the ox and the grey donkey"
"Çà, bergers, assemblons-nous": Title translation: "Here, shepherds, let us gather". Adapted from "Où s'en vont ces gais bergers".
"Venez divin Messie": Translated in English as "O Come, Divine Messiah".
"D'où viens-tu, bergère?": Title translation "Where are you coming from, shepherdess?"
"Dans cette étable": Title translation: "In this stable". It is sung to the same music as "Es ist ein Ros entsprungen"
